subject: BetaHealth private deploy — unit economics, env count, and support tiers (post-call)
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Green <sam.green@betahealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: BetaHealth private deploy — unit economics, env count, and support tiers (post-call)

Hi Sam — thanks for taking the call earlier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can put a preliminary commercial together. Notes below are from our side; please correct anything I mis-stated.

Call recap
- Use case: clinical summarization + chart ingestion for care teams (PHI retains on-prem or VPC).
- Target go-live for pilot: Q3 2028 (pilot 8–10 weeks).
- Environments: you indicated 3 distinct environments (prod, staging, dev) with separate VPCs for prod and staging.
- Latency SLO target: 200–300ms p95 for single-turn generation, bursts during peak clinic hours.

Commercial info we need to confirm
1) Monthly token volume (approx): you mentioned mid-single-digit billions per month — can you confirm an estimated range (low / expected / high)?
2) Peak TPS / concurrent requests: rough peak per-second rate during clinic hours?
3) Budget target expressed as $/1M tokens: you said the team is targeting a unit economic range — can you confirm a target $/1M tokens or a budget band?
4) Preferred licensing model: committed token blocks vs usage-only? Also confirm whether you need a per-environment license fee for air-gapped on-prem.
5) Support requirements: standard vs enterprise (24/7 + named CSM + escalation path) — which level do you expect?

Prelim commercial constructs (for discussion)
- Licensing: two primary paths — (A) committed monthly token package + discounted unit price; (B) pay-as-you-go with higher unit $ and no minimum.
- Environment fees: one-time on-prem environment setup fee (networking, packaging) and a small monthly infra management fee per environment.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours) vs Enterprise (24/7, technical account management, faster SLA credits).

Attachments: redwood-private-pricing-options.pdf (high-level constructs) and ma-terms-draft.docx (template). I'm also attaching a preliminary econ sheet after you confirm volumes.

Next steps
- Could you send the monthly token low/expected/high numbers and confirm the three envs?
- If you have an internal budget band (e.g., $/1M tokens target), share that so we can tune the proposal.
- Procurement contact? I'll loop them into the commercial thread once we have numbers.

Thanks — I can turn around a short proposal + two pricing options by EOD Monday once I have the numbers.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Follow-up: BetaHealth private deploy — unit economics, env count, and support tiers (post-call)

Thanks Rishi — appreciate the clear recap. Confirming numbers below so you can model the econ: 

Estimated volumes
- Monthly tokens: low 1.8B / expected 2.5B / high 3.6B
- Peak: ~55 concurrent requests, typical peak TPS ~12–15 (short bursts)
- Env count: 3 (Prod VPC isolated, Staging VPC isolated, Dev shared VPC) — Prod and Staging need separate control-plane connections; Dev can be lighter.

Budget and procurement
- Internal target band: $300–$400 per 1M tokens for the pilot stage. If infra or SLA add significant ops cost we could stretch to upper band but prefer to stay near $350/1M as a target.
- Procurement timeline: we expect internal approvals in 6–8 weeks post-proposal. Procurement contact is procurement@betahealth.ai (CC'd).

Support requirements
- For pilot we'll need Enterprise-level support (named CSM + escalation) because clinical uptime matters. For full rollout we may contract 24/7.

Security/compliance
- We will need SOC2 Type II evidence, encryption-at-rest + in-transit confirmation, and a short risk summary for our InfoSec.

If you can send two pricing options (committed vs usage) with the $/1M math and line items for env fees and support, we'll review with Procurement.

Thanks — Sam

Subject: Proposal sketch + unit-econ math (two options)

Sam / Procurement team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Attached is a short econ sheet (prelim-econ-sheet.xlsx) but below are the headline options so you have numbers inline: 

Assumptions (for math below): expected volume = 2.5B tokens/month

Option A — Committed monthly package
- Commit: 1.5B tokens/month @ $280 / 1M tokens = $420,000 / month
- Overage: $320 / 1M tokens on usage beyond commit
- Higher commit tier: 3.0B tokens/month @ $240 / 1M tokens (saves ~14%)

Option B — Pay-as-you-go (no commit)
- Unit price: $475 / 1M tokens
- No minimum, month-to-month usage tracking

Environment & infra fees
- One-time on-prem/VPC environment setup: $25,000 per dedicated env (covers packaging, network validation, air-gap prep).
- Monthly environment maintenance fee: $5,000 per prod/staging env; $1,200 for dev shared env.

Support tiers (pilot needs Enterprise)
- Standard support: included, business-hours, ticket SLA 8 hours
- Enterprise support: $12,500 / month — named CSM, 24/7 escalation, quarterly health reviews, 99.9% availability SLA with defined credits.

Example total (proxy) — expected 2.5B tokens, commit 1.5B:
- Token costs: $420k (commit) + overage 1.0B * $320/1M = $320k -> total token = $740k / month -> effective ~$296 / 1M tokens
- Env fees: one-time setup for Prod+Staging = $50k; monthly env fees = $5k + $5k + $1.2k = $11.2k
- Support: Enterprise $12.5k / month

Net effective unit: ~ $296 / 1M tokens for the first month (with 1.5B commit). If BetaHealth selects 3.0B commit the unit drops to ~$240 / 1M.

Next asks from our side
- Confirm whether BetaHealth prefers a smaller commit (1.5B) or a larger commit (3B) to price both paths formally.
- Confirm procurement timeline and whether Procurement wants the MSA redlines included now or after pricing.

I'll attach the econ sheet with a sensitivity table across commit sizes and env counts. If this direction looks good we'll scope a mutual action plan and include SOC2 artifacts and a short security Q/A.

Best,
Rishi

Attachment: prelim-econ-sheet.xlsx (sensitivity table for commit sizes / env-counts)
